body:
I amended the comment; I didn't know about the pre-commit checks until after I made the PR. Woops!

That said, I don't think "triggers" is right?
If `idle_parse` is disabled, it shouldn't start the timer https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/19bb18716ef08b811fec330cba4d35fbdb027bcc/editor/code_editor.cpp#L1012

A little background to this code:

Without this safeguard, there would be an infinite recursion (_then_ reproducible by  `ctrl`-clicking on a custom class inside a GDScript), caused by:

1. ScriptTextEditor::apply_code()
2. ScriptTextEditor::_validate_script()
3. ...??? (GDB's backtrace gets weird here, something to do with signals)
4. ScriptEditor::_update_script_names()
5. ScriptEditor::_go_to_tab()
6. ScriptTextEditor::apply_code()

I know this solution isn't perfect, but it prevents `apply_code()` from being called twice within the same callstack. I can't think of a real-world scenario where this would actually be necessary, as that would imply a recursion, which is precisely what this prevents.

This needs to check `editor_enabled`, since this is ran on all open scripts it happens on the ones that may not be fully loaded yet and will cause errors.
Though checking this wouldn't be needed after https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115662
This also will need to be called when TextEditor and TextShaderEditor get saved, since they also rely on the same settings.

I haven't been able to reproduce yet, but I can see it from the callstack.
This should be fixed by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/111309 which cleans up the script names function a bit.
This approach should be fine until then.
I think this should be above the idle_parse_delay settings since it controls them.

body: Also fair. Thank you!
Reasonable, I just didn't dare to place my shiny new setting at the top. 😛 Makes sense, though.

Huh, so that's why I was experiencing hiccups when saving with multiple large GDScripts opened...

I just recompiled Godot with that change and now the hiccup is much less noticeable even on the largest script - I presume because it's only validating the active/shown script. Neat!

Good catch, the shader editor still relies entirely on the idle parsing.

On a somewhat related note, I discovered that the shader editor exclusively uses the idle parse delay (and not the error idle parse delay) - even when errors are found. Presumably this is a bug? If so, I reckon it should be tracked under a separate issue to avoid scope creep within this PR.

**EDIT:** I forgot to ask - do you have any pointers for which functions would be involved in the saving of the shader editor? If not I can definitely take a look on my own, though no sooner than Monday, as my week-end schedule's a little packed :sweat_smile:

body: In the documentation, it should always sorted alphabetically regardless of actual order. This is the error in the CI.

The shader editor probably should be using the error idle parse delay, I'll look into it. I agree it should be fixed separately. It probably also happens for the text editor.

For shader editor, probably `TextShaderEditor::save_external_data` or `apply_shaders`.

The text editor also needs it in `apply_code`. Json files can have errors too.

I'm struggling to find a place where I can safely make a call to `_validate_script()` for the shader editor. I've checked the backtraces with GDB and found that both idle parsing and manual saving eventually lead to the same segment of function calls, but only idle parsing goes through `_validate_script()`, which is what triggers the GUI to redraw and show errors.

I attached the two stack traces leading up to `ShaderTextEditor::_shader_changed()`, perhaps you (or somebody else) can find a clever way to approach this without causing recursions?

[backtrace_via_ctrl_s.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26160990/backtrace_via_ctrl_s.txt)
[backtrace_via_idle_parse_delay.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26160991/backtrace_via_idle_parse_delay.txt)
